questions.q: Why does the capstone regression model the logarithm of units instead of raw units?
options: Logs make the sealed test set larger
Statsmodels cannot fit raw units
A promotion raises demand by a percentage, so a coefficient on the log scale reads as a percent change
Logs remove the need for a backtest
questions.explain: On a log scale, exp(coefficient) - 1 is the percent change, which matches how promotions and holidays affect demand.

questions.q: Why does the boosting model fit a straight-line trend first and learn only what is left?
options: Tree-based models cannot extrapolate a trend beyond the values seen in training
Boosting cannot use a promo flag directly
It makes the model slower on purpose
It replaces the need for cross-validation
questions.explain: Trees predict averages of training values, so a rising level would be capped. Removing the trend first and adding it back solves that.

questions.q: What does the calendar-only model (trend and season, no promo or holiday flags) scoring 93.7, about the same as naive, tell us?
options: The seasonal wave is the main driver of the gain
Nearly all the improvement comes from knowing the planned promotion and holiday calendar
Regression never works on weekly data
The backtest was run on the sealed test set
questions.explain: Adding the promo and holiday inputs cut MAE from about 94 to about 30, so the forecast is only as good as the promo plan supplied.

questions.q: The lesson compares regression coefficients with SHAP values from the boosting model. What does agreement between them show?
options: That the models are causal proofs
That the boosting model is always better
That SHAP values are measured in units, not log units
Two different methods tell the same story about the promotion effect (about 30%), which makes the explanation more credible
questions.explain: The regression gave 31.1% and SHAP implied about 30.5%. Agreement across methods increases confidence, though neither by itself proves causation.

questions.q: Why is has_constant="add" used with sm.add_constant on a 13-week test window?
options: A window with no holiday has an all-zero column, which could be mistaken for a constant and the intercept skipped
It scales all columns to mean zero
It removes the promo column
It makes the forecast log-scaled
questions.explain: Without it, statsmodels may treat an existing constant column as the intercept and not add one, leaving the design matrix without an intercept column, so predictions fail or come out wrong.
